title: The Async Pipe & Advanced Patterns ⚡
description: Use the async pipe to subscribe to Observables and Promises directly in the template.

slides.title: The Magic of Async Pipe 🪄
slides.content:
# Handle Asynchronous Data the Angular Way

The `async` pipe subscribes to an `Observable` or `Promise` and returns the latest value. It also automatically unsubscribes when the component is destroyed.

```html
{{ myObservable$ | async }}
```

* No manual subscription management.
* No risk of memory leaks.
* Works with `ngIf`, `ngFor`, and any expression.

slides.title: Async Pipe with HttpClient
slides.content:
When you call `http.get()` you get an Observable. Use async pipe directly instead of subscribing in the component: ```typescript // Component users$ = this.http.get('/api/users'); ``` ```html

slides.title: Async Pipe and Change Detection ⚠️
slides.content: The async pipe marks the component for check when a new value arrives. It works seamlessly with `OnPush` change detection strategy – making your app much faster.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `async` pipe with `OnPush` for Max Performance

Set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` on your component. The async pipe will trigger change detection only when new data arrives, drastically reducing checks.

quizData.question: The `async` pipe can subscribe to both Observables and ________.
quizData.explanation: Async pipe works with both Observables and Promises.
